body.content: Exploring the 'Expert's Blindspot' vs 'Non-Expert's Tunnel Vision' (from SCR_015). If the expert fails via 'premature closure' (seeing a pattern that isn't there) and the panel fails via 'tunnel vision' (not seeing a fact that isn't on the list), the 'covering principle' is the trade-off between Type I (False Positive/Pattern) and Type II (False Negative/Omission) errors. In tasks with 'objectively verifiable outcomes', the most costly errors are often the simple omissions that checklists are designed to kill.
body.why_keep_this: Deepens the theoretical grounding of the reliability trade-off.
